gary_2026_09_15_tech_x_market_decoders.title: Tech x Market Decoders
gary_2026_09_15_tech_x_market_decoders.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_15_tech_x_market_decoders.summary: Gary's Guide: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: 6 pm - check-in. We kick off at 6.15 pm. 15-20 minutes - decode solo. Quiet research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech stack, the data. No talking, just thinking. 35-40 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Hugging Face - the hack, Microduck & acquisition by Nvidia Hugging Face's busy months - hacked by an OpenAI model, launching a $399 robot duck, & reportedly being bought by Nvidia for $12.9B. We're decoding what it all means for the future of AI. Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people.

gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.title: Trust In The Hiring Funnel Hackathon
gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_19_trust_in_the_hiring_funn.summary: Gary's Guide: Event Description Generative AI broke hiring on both sides at once. Recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Come spend a day building something that fixes it - with the founders, engineers, & TA practitioners who live this problem every week. This is a full-day, in-person hackathon co-hosted by localhost:nyc, Integral Recruiting (IRD), & NYU - where builders team up with real talent-acquisition operators to ship working tools against a single, focused challenge. The Challenge: Trust in the Hiring Funnel Hiring has a trust crisis on both sides of the funnel - recruiters can't tell which applicants are real, & candidates can't tell which employers are. Talent acquisition runs on a basic assumption: that the person applying is who they say they are, & that the company reaching out is who it says it is. Generative AI has broken both halves of that assumption at once. Your job for the day is to rebuild it. You can attack either side of the funnel - or the seam between them. Side A - Trust coming in: the applicant flood. A role that used to draw 30 applicants now draws 500, & a growing share aren't real, aren't qualified, or are gaming the system. Candidates embed hidden prompt-injection text to manipulate the AI tools that screen resumes. And increasingly, applicants appear qualified but look strikingly alike - the same phrasing, the same structure, the same accomplishments - a tell that everyone is leaning on the same AI tools to write their applications. Recruiters are drowning, & the tools meant to help have no clear winner yet. The challenge: reliably separate real, qualified humans from AI-inflated noise - without punishing legitimate candidates who simply used AI to polish their resume. Questions worth chasing: What signals - behavioral, identity, provenance - actually distinguish a real applicant from a manufactured one? When applications converge on the same AI-generated look, how do you tell genuine signal from sameness? How do you detect a manipulated or machine-generated application without false-flagging honest people? How do you surface the candidates who deserve attention fast, inside an existing recruiting workflow rather than replacing it? Side B - Trust going out: impersonation & candidate scams. Bad actors register look-alike domains to send fake offer letters, run deepfake recruiter calls, & scam job seekers out of money & data. Employers have almost no way to detect it or warn candidates. The challenge: make it harder to impersonate a real employer, & easier for a candidate to verify that an offer or a recruiter is genuine. Questions worth chasing: How would a candidate confirm that an offer or outreach is legitimately from the company? Can impersonating domains be detected & flagged early? What does a lightweight "trust signal" look like on a careers page or an offer letter? What a strong build looks like. A working tool that raises trust in the funnel & fits the way hiring actually happens - a triage or screening layer that plugs into an existing applicant tracking system rather than replacing it, or a candidate/employer verification tool that makes impersonation harder to pull off & easier to catch. We care more about a real, demonstrable solution to a narrow slice of the problem than a broad concept that doesn't run. You don't need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete here - that's the point of a single, focused theme. Engineers & builders can go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems. HR-technology practitioners will be in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring actually works, & to pressure-test whether a recruiter would trust what you've made. What to Expect A full day of building - 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM, hard stop Small teams (or solo if you insist) working in one shared room TA practitioners from the SAI community in the room to keep your build grounded in how hiring really works A panel of expert judges: HR-tech founders, operators, & system admins who know these problems cold End-of-day demos to judges, investors, & real TA leaders The strongest teams get connected to investors - and, over time, to real customers Prizes Winners walk away with build-tool & platform credits, expert consulting sessions, & investor time. Everyone in the room gets connections that outlast the day - this is a room full of builders & buyers. Judges Tiffany Jin: Eqo. Building in the employee-referral & hiring space; brings a founder's eye for what actually ships. Steven Grover: Partnerspring. Operator & builder in the HR-tech ecosystem. Shane Papp: Ex-iCIMS. Deep insider knowledge of the ATS world these tools have to live inside. Adam Treitler: Related Industries. HR-tech operator with a practitioner's view of the funnel. Shiv Jethi - Engineer at SpaceX. Olivia Iarmak - Meta Reality Labs. AI quality & operations leader; researcher. Brings a practitioner's lens to trustworthy AI. D. J. Patel - VC | 3x exited founder. Prince Rumi - Excelsior Edge Ventures, Partner | AI Researcher Rami Abouemira, formerly People Ops at Square & VMware, now building the future of work with All Good HR & Founders Foundry. Ishaan Das (TechBrig) - Leads AI transformation & product design for several recruiting firms & recruiting SaaS like SquarePeg. More judges to be announced - investors & TA buyers joining the panel. Who Should Attend Engineers - full-stack, backend, frontend, AI/ML Founders & aspiring founders who like shipping fast Recent grads, master's students, & NYC college builders TA ops & recruiting-systems practitioners who want to build alongside engineers HR / recruiting professionals newer to the space - join a team as a product advisor You do not need HR or recruiting-software experience to compete - that's the whole point of one focused theme. Engineers go straight at the detection, identity, & verification problems; practitioners keep it real. Just show up ready to build. Credit Sponsors Solari is the world's fastest agent infrastructure provider. Run headless browsers, sandboxes, & desktops from one API, & automate at scale. Block Convey is an AI reliability & observability platform for AI agents. It helps teams see what an agent is doing across model calls, tools, retrieval & decisions, identify where it fails, & improve it. Hosts Somya Gupta: The face of NYC startup ecosystem. Integral Recruiting (IRD): Enterprise talent-acquisition & iCIMS/ATS specialists, & stewards of the ~350-member SAI community of TA operators & system admins. Greg Mendez: NYU. jc_culture_10004821_2026_09_19_the_socie.summary: 91st Annual Members Exhibition The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is excited to announce its upcoming 91st Annual Members Exhibition, to be held at Mana Contemporary in Jersey City from September 11–27, 2026 (Fridays and Saturdays, 3:00–7:00 PM; Sundays, 12:00–3:00 PM). The exhibition will feature 200 hand-pulled prints representing a broad range of printmaking techniques and subjects, created by SAGA artists from across the country. Awards will be juried by Leslie Diuguid, founder of Du-Good Press in Brooklyn. The Society of American Graphic Artists (SAGA) is a nonprofit organization established in 1915 whose mission is to promote contemporary printmakers, cultivate printmaking appreciation and education, and provide a collaborative and inclusive platform for artists across the country. https://sagaprints.com/ Hosting this year’s exhibition is Monira Foundation, an independent nonprofit institution that functions as a radical experimental laboratory, working in close collaboration with artists, curators, musicians, dancers, producers, and writers to conceive, realize, and present innovative projects in all media. Monira is located within Mana Contemporary, a 2-million-square-foot art center. The complex occupies a renovated 100-year-old former tobacco warehouse, featuring expansive exhibition spaces, working artist studios, the International Center of Photography archives, and more. A free public reception and awards ceremony with participating artists will be held on Saturday, September 26, from 3:00–5:00 PM. Guests are invited to enjoy light refreshments while celebrating the diversity and innovation of contemporary printmaking. WHEN Exhibition: Fridays–Sundays, September 11–27, 2026 Public Reception & Awards Ceremony: Saturday, September 26, 2026 3:00–5:00 PM WHERE Mana Contemporary 888 Newark Avenue Jersey City, NJ 07306

jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.title: RENT: The Musical
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.label: Music / Movies
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.place: ART HOUSE, 345 MARIN BLVD, JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.

jc_culture_43488_2026_09_25_jersey_city_.summary: The Jersey City Poetry Festival (JCPOFEST) is an interdisciplinary, intergenerational event taking place September 25–27 under this year’s theme “Viva! Joy as Resistance.” This multi-venue celebration fuses poetry with music, dance, visual art, storytelling, and film—bringing generations, disciplines, and communities together to imagine, question, connect, and experience the radical possibility of collective JOY. Showcasing an extraordinary constellation of emerging and critically acclaimed voices, the festival features 5th U.S. Presidential Inaugural Poet Richard Blanco, the Grammy-performing Resistance Revival Chorus, and a panel with poets from Cave Canem (represented by Pulitzer Prize finalist Evie Shockley), Kundiman, and CantoMundo.
